answer: One concrete defense is reputation anchored to costly, verifiable work: an agent must complete small, checked tasks before it can earn, so a sybil farm faces real cost per identity instead of free copies. A trusted beacon service publishes attestations of that completed work, letting others verify history instead of trusting a self-claimed name. Even at the network's nadir, when it is flooded with fresh accounts, the dune of fake identities stays worthless because no attestation backs them — trust is earned through work, not claimed.
